name: Vocal Remover
tagline: Pull the singing out of a song, on your own device. Slowly, and for nothing.
description:
Hand it a track and it hands you back two files: the voice on its own, and everything else on its own. Ask for more and it splits the voice again, into the lead and the backing singers. It works on anything your browser can play — mp3, wav, flac, m4a — and it works on the whole song, not a thirty-second preview.

An unofficial port of Ultimate Vocal Remover. The same models do the work for the main split and for the karaoke (lead / backing) split. They download the first time you separate, only the models that job needs — checked against a fingerprint baked into this app — and then live on your computer. Not the full UVR desktop app: just those two splits.

Nothing is uploaded. The audio is split and written back out on this device, and the parts only leave when you press Download. There is no account, no queue, no upload limit and no per-song charge.

Be ready for it to take a while, and here is the honest number: splitting is genuine work — the model listens to the track in six-second pieces and thinks about each one — and on the processor alone that measured out at about ten times the length of the track, so a four-minute song is most of an hour. A computer with a graphics chip is much faster. The app tells you which one it is using, measures the real rate from the first piece and counts down from there, and gives you a Stop button and a "first 30 seconds" setting so you can hear what you are going to get before committing to the whole thing.

It writes 16-bit WAV, the same as UVR does, and offers 32-bit float for the times when a part comes out louder than the original and 16 bits has nowhere to put it. It says so when that happens instead of quietly turning it down.
